selection: From the frozen TTF S1 cohort of 239 butterflies with >0 host family breadth and native host-region coverage, remove the original 11-species GloBI pilot, and sample exactly 10 species uniformly at random without replacement from each of Hesperiidae, Lycaenidae, Nymphalidae, Papilionidae and Pieridae. Riodinidae is exhausted by the original pilot.
randomization: Python random.Random(20261008) over alphabetically sorted candidate species for each alphabetically sorted family, no substitution if zero observations
query: GloBI interaction.csv: sourceTaxon=frozen species; interactionType=eats; includeObservations=true; two pages x 512 records per species; stop if page partial; archive raw pages and record checksum; cap or error as unknown not zero
observational_evidence: Restrict to observations dated 1800-2025, georeferenced exact WGSRPD3, explicitly larval, herbivory relation, non-HOSTS provenance, plant species accepted in frozen HOSTS-WCVP. iNaturalist original specimen IDs are mandatory for direct evidence subset.
outcome: How many independently evidenced butterfly×introduced-host×WGSRPD3 interactions occur in introduced-only resource cells; report number of butterfly species and areas, native butterfly geography status not inferred from records.
gate: Exploratory source coverage credible if introduced-only direct records occur across >=3 held-out species and >=3 regions, with no capped species hidden as reliable zeros; then manually check native butterfly range and host-alternative completeness. Passing does not prove colonization or fitness.
stopping_rule: If source coverage is too sparse, do not infer ecological absence and stop using GloBI feeding-positive records to claim butterfly range filling. Do not adaptively replace sampled species.
previous_pilot: 11 species panel yielded 45 purported introduced-only host use records, 1 original taxon contradiction, 1 native Caribbean case with omitted known native host link; not counted as confirmation.
